title.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: a locally compact group acting faithfully on a connected $n$-manifold is a Lie group, for every $n$

plain: Any group that moves a space around continuously and faithfully is a smooth one, like the rotations of a ball

beats.text: Known in dimensions 1 and 2, and in dimension 3 since Pardon. Never above
Everything reduces to the $p$-adic integers $\mathbb Z_p$ acting faithfully
A signature-like class would split into $p^k$ equal lattice parts. It cannot

steps: Every bad case boils down to one kind of infinitely fine symmetry
That symmetry would split one fixed quantity into $p^k$ equal whole parts
Too many equal parts cannot fit the lattice: the action cannot exist

achievement.label: Hilbert–Smith conjecture (Smith, 1940s)
statement: G \curvearrowright M^n \text{ faithfully} \ \Rightarrow\ G \text{ is a Lie group}
achievement.context: Before: dimensions 1 to 3 (Pardon 2013), and Lipschitz, quasiconformal or Hölder actions
achievement.note: A new sheaf-theoretic invariant, with nothing in Lean

verify.detail: Manuscript only: 46 pages for a problem about eighty years old
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Known up to dimension three. Everything reduces to the p-adic integers acting faithfully.
Such an action would split one quantity into too many equal parts.
Claimed: every such group is a Lie group.

sources.quote: Dimensions 1-2 classical; dimension 3 proved by Pardon (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2013).
Posed as the action form of Hilbert's fifth problem (Smith, 1940s).
No unrestricted proof in dimension >= 4 before this.
a faithful Z_p-action would split one class into p^k equal integral parts summing to 4u, impossible once p^k exceeds four times the lattice denominator.
A faithful action would split one class into $p^k$ equal integral parts summing to $4u_d$, and once $p^k > 4L_d$ that is impossible.
plus under regularity assumptions (Lipschitz, quasiconformal, Hölder)
